question: How much does a stand-alone, exact, half-anchor masked vote add to a deployable half-prefix plus one guard refit?
when: Timing correction after inspecting shared component times. Policies, cohort and support choices are fixed by budgeted_guard. No outcome-dependent changes.
arms: Half-prefix alone constructs only its prefix. Half-vote uses identical up-to-eight candidates and Gain order, screening with the separating minimum; prune a candidate as soon as its running minimum is <= its tie-winning incumbent, skip remaining candidates when best is four. Both compute the Compact Gain anchor from scratch, then compare candidate and anchor using one guard fit per distinct support, fit final on development and predict outer rows. At a singleton anchor skip both candidate and guard. Verify nominees, final supports, probabilities against archived complete minima.
timing: Data already in memory; wall and process seconds from first inner imputation through final outer predictions, including selection metrics and decisions. Excludes Python startup, file I/O, archived assertions and benchmarking logs. XGBoost one thread, bind process to logical CPU 2 when available, following the earlier timing protocol. Per fold two order-balanced pairs (AB then BA or BA then AB depending on fold plus task index). Fresh models and caches for every arm. Per fold use average of the two elapsed times of each policy, average within task and then across tasks; also report median paired task-level ratio. No runtime equivalence test on single host.
cohorts: All 41 eligible PMLB folds; Optdigits measured separately. Do not combine benchmarks. One-hour maximum for each worker.
